level_1: Gathers information strictly following a template
level_2: Adapts template to filter and prioritize pertinent positives and negatives based on broad diagnostic categories or possible diagnoses
level_3: Filters, prioritizes, and synthesizes the history to develop a differential diagnosis in real-time for uncomplicated or typical presentations
level_4: Filters, prioritizes, and synthesizes the history to develop a differential diagnosis in real time for complicated or atypical presentations
level_5: Recognizes and probes subtle clues from patients and families; distinguishes nuances among diagnoses to efficiently drive further information gathering

level_1: Performs fundamental physical examination
Performs a physical examination with consistent use of a developmentally appropriate approach
level_2: Performs a rote physical examination using a strict head-to-toe approach
Performs complete or focused physical examination, as indicated, and selects advanced maneuvers to distinguish between diagnoses
level_3: Performs complete physical examination and identifies variants and abnormal findings
Performs a physical examination using strategies to maximize patient cooperation and comfort
level_4: Performs a physical examination considering appropriate adaptation for age and development
Detects, pursues, and integrates key physical examination findings to distinguish nuances among competing, often similar diagnoses
level_5: Performs complete or focused physical examination, as indicated, and interprets normal variants and abnormal findings
Performs a physical examination that consistently and positively engages the patient

level_1: Completes tasks for an individual patient, when prompted
level_2: Organizes patient care responsibilities by focusing on individual (rather than multiple) patients
level_3: Organizes and prioritizes the simultaneous care of patients with efficiency
level_4: Organizes, prioritizes, and delegates patient care responsibilities even when patient volume approaches the capacity of the individual or facility; anticipates and triages urgent and emergent issues
level_5: Serves as a role model and coach for patient care responsibilities

level_1: Presents clinical facts (e.g., history, exam, tests, consultations) in the order they were elicited
level_2: Generates an unfocused differential diagnosis based on the clinical facts
level_3: Organizes clinical facts to compare and contrast diagnoses being considered, resulting in a prioritized differential diagnosis
level_4: Integrates clinical facts into a unifying diagnosis(es); reappraises in real time to avoid diagnostic error
level_5: Role models and coaches the organization of clinical facts to develop a prioritized differential diagnosis, including life threatening diagnoses, atypical presentations, and complex clinical presentations

level_1: Reports management plans developed by others
level_2: Participates in the creation of management plans
level_3: Develops an interdisciplinary management plan for common and typical diagnoses
level_4: Develops and implements informed management plans for complicated and atypical diagnoses, with the ability to modify plans as necessary
level_5: Serves as a role model and coach for development of management plans for complicated and atypical diagnoses, with the ability to modify plans as necessary

level_1: Demonstrates basic medical knowledge
level_2: Links basic medical knowledge to clinical scenarios
level_3: Applies medical knowledge to common and typical scenarios to guide patient care
level_4: Integrates a breadth of medical knowledge that includes complicated and atypical conditions to guide patient care
level_5: Teaches at multiple levels, drawing from a breadth of medical knowledge that spans the continuum of simple to complex problems

level_1: Lists basic evaluation (e.g., diagnostic testing and consultation) for common diagnoses, with prompting
Interprets clinical significance of diagnostic study results
level_2: Reports results of diagnostic studies
Prioritizes and optimizes evaluation based on risks, benefits, indications, and alternatives to clarify the diagnosis(es)
level_3: Recommends broad evaluation based on an unfocused differential diagnosis
Interprets clinical significance of diagnostic study results while considering study limitations
level_4: Identifies clinically significant diagnostic study results, with guidance
Educates others about risks, benefits, indications, and alternatives to guide diagnostic decision making
level_5: Recommends focused evaluation based on a prioritized differential diagnosis
Teaches others to interpret clinically significant results and consider study limitations

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
level_3: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Discloses patient safety events to patients and families (simulated or actual)
level_4: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (simulated or actual)
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_5: Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Role models or mentors others in the disclosure of patient safety events

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
level_2: Describes local quality improvement initiatives (e.g., community vaccination rate, infection rate, smoking cessation)
level_3: Participates in local quality improvement initiatives
level_4: Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_5: Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community level

subcompetencies.name: System Navigation for Patient Centered Care – Coordination of Care

level_1: Lists the various interprofessional individuals involved in the patient’s care coordination
level_2: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations, incorporating interprofessional teams with consideration of patient and family needs
level_3: Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations, effectively utilizing the roles of interprofessional teams, and incorporating patient and family needs and goals
level_4: Coordinates interprofessional, patient-centered care among different disciplines and specialties, actively assisting families in navigating the health- care system
level_5: Coaches others in interprofessional, patient- centered care coordination

subcompetencies.name: System Navigation for Patient-Centered Care – Transitions in Care

level_1: Uses a standard template for transitions of care/hand-offs
level_2: Adapts a standard template, recognizing key elements for safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations
level_3: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations, and ensures closed-loop communication
level_4: Performs and advocates for safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs within and across health care delivery systems, including transitions to adult care
level_5: Coaches others in improving transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes

level_1: Demonstrates awareness of population and community health needs
level_2: Identifies specific population and community health needs; identifies local resources
level_3: Uses local resources effectively to meet the needs of a patient population and community
level_4: Adapts practice to provide for the needs of a specific population
level_5: Advocates at the local, regional, or national level for populations and communities with health care needs

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Engages with patients and other providers in discussions about cost- conscious care and key components of the health care delivery system
level_2: Identifies the relationships between the delivery system and cost- conscious care and the impact on the patient care
level_3: Discusses the need for changes in clinical approaches based on evidence, outcomes, and cost-effectiveness to improve care for patients and families
level_4: Advocates for the promotion of safe, quality, and high-value care
level_5: Coaches others to promote safe, quality, and high-value care across health care systems

level_1: Develops an answerable clinical question and demonstrates how to access available evidence, with guidance
level_2: Independently articulates clinical question and accesses available evidence
level_3: Locates and applies the evidence, integrated with patient preference, to the care of patients
level_4: Critically appraises and applies evidence, even in the face of uncertainty and conflicting evidence to guide care tailored to the individual patient
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex patients

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Participates in feedback sessions
Designs and implements a learning plan by analyzing and reflecting on the factors which contribute to gap(s) between performance expectations and actual performance
level_2: Develops personal and professional goals, with assistance
Seeks and incorporates feedback and performance data consistently
level_3: Demonstrates openness to feedback and performance data
Adapts a learning plan using long-term professional goals, self- reflection, and performance data to measure its effectiveness
level_4: Designs a learning plan based on established goals, feedback, and performance data, with assistance
Role models and coaches others in seeking and incorporating feedback and performance data
level_5: Seeks and incorporates feedback and performance data episodically
Demonstrates continuous self-reflection and coaching of others on reflective practice

level_1: Identifies expected professional behaviors and potential triggers for lapses
Fully engages in patient care and holds oneself accountable
level_2: Identifies the value and role of pediatrics as a vocation/career
Recognizes situations that may trigger professionalism lapses and intervenes to prevent lapses in self and others
level_3: Demonstrates professional behavior with occasional lapses
Exhibits a sense of duty to patient care and professional responsibilities
level_4: Demonstrates accountability for patient care as a pediatrician, with guidance
Models professional behavior and coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_5: Maintains professional behavior in increasingly complex or stressful situations
Extends the role of the pediatrician beyond the care of patients by engaging with the community, specialty, and medical profession as a whole

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of the ethical principles underlying informed consent, surrogate decision making, advance directives, confidentiality, error disclosure, stewardship of limited resources, and related topics
level_2: Applies ethical principles in common situations
level_3: Analyzes complex situations using ethical principles to address conflict/controversy; seeks help when needed to manage and resolve complex ethical situations
level_4: Manages and seeks to resolve ethical dilemmas using appropriate resources (e.g., ethics consultations, literature review, risk management/legal consultation)
level_5: Called upon by others to consult in cases of complex ethical dilemmas; identifies and seeks to address system- level factors that induce or exacerbate

level_1: Performs tasks and responsibilities, with prompting
level_2: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner in routine situations
level_3: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a thorough and timely manner in complex or stressful situations
level_4: Coaches others to ensure tasks and responsibilities are completed in a thorough and timely manner in complex or stressful situations
level_5: Creates strategies to enhance others’ ability to efficiently complete tasks and responsibilities

level_1: Recognizes the importance of addressing personal and professional well-being
level_2: Describes institutional resources that are meant to promote well-being
level_3: Recognizes institutional and personal factors that impact well-being
level_4: Describes interactions between institutional and personal factors that impact well-being
level_5: Coaches and supports colleagues to optimize well-being at the team, program, or institutional level

level_1: Demonstrates respect and attempts to establish rapport
Communicates with sensitivity and compassion, elicits patient/family values, and acknowledges uncertainty and conflict
level_2: Attempts to adjust communication strategies based upon patient/family expectations
Establishes a therapeutic relationship in straightforward and complex encounters, including those with ambiguity and/or conflict
level_3: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in straightforward encounters
Uses shared decision making with patient/family to make a personalized care plan
level_4: Adjusts communication strategies as needed to mitigate barriers and meet patient/family expectations
Mentors others to develop positive therapeutic relationships
level_5: Establishes a culturally aware and therapeutic relationship in most encounters
Models and coaches others in patient- and family-centered communication

level_1: Respectfully requests a consultation, with guidance
Uses bi-directional communication within the interprofessional team
level_2: Identifies the members of the interprofessional team
Coordinates consultant recommendations to optimize patient care
level_3: Clearly and concisely requests consultation by communicating patient information
Facilitates interprofessional team communication
level_4: Participates within the interprofessional team
Maintains a collaborative relationship with referring providers that maximizes adherence to practice recommendations
level_5: Formulates a specific question for consultation and tailors communication strategy
Coaches others in effective communication within the interprofessional team

level_1: Records accurate information in the patient record
Aligns type of communication with message to be delivered (e.g., direct and indirect) based on urgency and complexity
level_2: Identifies the importance of and responds to multiple forms of communication (e.g., in- person, electronic health record (EHR), telephone, email)
Documents diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning, including anticipatory guidance
level_3: Records accurate and timely information in the patient record
Demonstrates exemplary written and verbal communication
level_4: Selects appropriate method of communication, with prompting
Models and coaches others in documenting diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning
level_5: Concisely documents updated, prioritized, diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning in the patient record
Coaches others in written and verbal communication
